claims.claim: A sidereal day on Venus — one full rotation, 243.025 Earth days — is longer than its year, the 224.70 Earth days it takes to orbit the Sun
claims.definition: Sidereal rotation period vs orbital period of Venus; the standard NASA planetary data comparison
claims.measured_value: rotation 243.025 Earth days (retrograde); orbital period 224.70 Earth days
claims.authoritative_source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet (NSSDC); NASA Science - Venus Facts; NASA Space Place
claims.notes: Narration rounds to 243 and 225. Solar day (sunrise to sunrise) is a different quantity - see venus_solar_day_117.

claims.claim: Venus completes a full orbit of the Sun before it completes a single rotation
claims.definition: Computed comparison: orbital period 224.70 d < sidereal rotation 243.025 d; 243.025/224.70 = 1.08 orbits per sidereal day
claims.authoritative_source: Computed from NASA Planetary Fact Sheet periods
claims.notes: Explicitly computed, not a measured record.

claims.claim: Venus rotates retrograde — backwards relative to its orbital direction and the spin of most planets
claims.definition: Retrograde rotation; Venus's axial spin is opposite its orbital motion
claims.authoritative_source: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet; NASA Space Place - All About Venus

claims.claim: On Venus the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east
claims.definition: Direct consequence of retrograde rotation viewed from the surface
claims.measured_value: apparent solar path across the sky is reversed vs Earth
claims.authoritative_source: NASA Space Place - All About Venus; NASA Science - Venus Facts

claims.claim: A solar day on Venus, sunrise to sunrise, is about 117 Earth days
claims.definition: Solar day combines retrograde rotation with orbital motion; measured 116.75 Earth days
claims.authoritative_source: NASA Space Place; UCLA radar-speckle rotation study published in Science (2021)
claims.notes: Distinct from the 243.025-day sidereal rotation. Narration uses the standard ~117 figure.

claims.claim: A Venus year passes between barely two sunrises
claims.definition: Computed: 224.70 d year / 116.75 d solar day = 1.92 solar days per year
claims.authoritative_source: Computed from NASA periods (orbital 224.70 d, solar day 116.75 d)

claims.claim: The cause of Venus's slow retrograde spin is not settled; leading hypotheses include an ancient giant impact and atmospheric tidal drag
claims.definition: Open scientific question; narration stays hedged ('may have') and presents no mechanism as fact
claims.authoritative_source: NASA Science - Venus; JPL public materials on Venus rotation
claims.notes: Deliberately hedged beat - the payoff keeps the mystery open rather than asserting a mechanism.
